# Special cases of the TDMS format

<!-- generated by `just catalogue` from tests/catalogue.py and tests/testcases.py: do not edit -->

77 special cases, exercised by 80 synthetic files (`tests/testcases.py`), 4 real files (`tests/data/real`) and a few behaviour tests.

## The file

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `file.minimal` | A file of one segment with one group and one channel is read. | `minimal` |
| `file.empty_is_error` | A file of 0 bytes, or shorter than a lead-in (28 bytes), is a `TdmsFormatError`. | `empty_file`, `shorter_than_lead_in` |
| `file.wrong_signature_is_error` | A file that does not start with `TDSm` is a `TdmsFormatError` (not a crash, not a guess). | `wrong_signature` |
| `file.index_file_is_error` | A `.tdms_index` file (signature `TDSh`) is refused with a clear message: it holds no data. | `index_file` |
| `file.not_tdms_inside` | A segment with a wrong signature after valid ones is a `TdmsFormatError`, unless it is the cut-off end of the file. | `garbage_after_segments` |

## Versions

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `version.4712` | Segments of version 4712 (TDMS 1.0) are read. | `version_4712` |
| `version.4713` | Segments of version 4713 (TDMS 2.0) are read. | `minimal`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `version.unknown_is_error` | Any other version number is a `TdmsFormatError`. | `version_unknown` |

## Segments

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `segment.many` | Hundreds of small segments of one channel are read as one continuous channel, in order. | `many_segments`, `many_segments_5000`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `segment.metadata_only` | A segment without raw data (no raw data flag) defines objects and properties and adds no values. | `metadata_only_segment` |
| `segment.raw_only` | A segment without metadata (no metadata flag) holds more data for the previous segment's objects, layout and indexes. | `raw_only_segment` |
| `segment.meta_without_new_list` | A segment with metadata but without the new-object-list flag updates only the objects it lists; every other object keeps its index and still receives its share of the raw data. | `meta_without_new_list`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `segment.new_list_replaces` | A new object list replaces the active one: an object left out gets no more data in that segment, one added gets some. | `new_list_replaces` |
| `segment.raw_offset_padding` | The raw data starts where the lead-in's raw data offset says, even if the metadata is shorter. | `raw_offset_padding` |
| `segment.zero_values` | A channel whose index says 0 values (or a segment with an empty raw data section) adds nothing and breaks nothing. | `zero_values` |
| `segment.next_offset_unknown` | A last segment whose next segment offset is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF (still being written) runs to the end of the file. | `next_offset_unknown` |
| `segment.truncated_file` | A file cut off inside its last segment gives the complete values of that segment and sets `file.truncated`; `strict=True` raises instead. | `truncated_mid_values`, `truncated_in_metadata`, `truncated_in_lead_in`, `truncated_interleaved_row`, `truncated_second_channel`, `truncated_after_whole_chunks` |
| `segment.next_offset_beyond_end` | A last segment declaring more bytes than the file has is treated as truncated. | `next_offset_beyond_end` |
| `segment.chunks` | A segment whose raw data is several repeats of the channel set (chunks) gives all the values, in order. | `chunks`, `truncated_after_whole_chunks`, `interleaved_chunks` |
| `segment.partial_chunk` | Bytes after the last whole chunk of a truncated segment give the values that are complete, none that are cut. | `truncated_mid_values`, `truncated_interleaved_row`, `truncated_second_channel` |

## The raw data index

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `index.none` | An index of 0xFFFFFFFF means the object has no data in this segment (and is not an error). | `metadata_only_segment`, `index_none_then_data`, `channel_without_data` |
| `index.same_as_previous` | An index of 0 means the previous segment's type and count for that channel. | `many_segments`, `index_same_after_change`, `mixed_endianness`, `property_update`, `many_segments_5000`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `index.changed_count` | A new explicit index changes a channel's count in a later segment. | `meta_without_new_list`, `zero_values`, `index_same_after_change` |
| `index.string` | The string index (type, dimension, count, total size) is read. | `strings` |
| `index.type_change_is_error` | A channel whose data type changes between segments is a `TdmsFormatError`. | `index_type_change` |
| `index.same_without_previous_is_error` | An index of 0 for a channel that never had an explicit one is a `TdmsFormatError`. | `index_same_without_previous` |

## The layout of the raw data

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `layout.contiguous_multi_channel` | Channels of one chunk are stored one after the other, each with its own count. | `truncated_second_channel`, `contiguous_three_types`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms` |
| `layout.unequal_counts` | Channels in one segment may have different counts (contiguous layout). | `unequal_counts`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `layout.interleaved` | Interleaved data (one value of each channel after the other) is read. | `truncated_interleaved_row`, `interleaved_two_channels`, `interleaved_three_channels_floats`, `big_endian_interleaved` |
| `layout.interleaved_chunks` | Interleaved data in several chunks is read. | `interleaved_chunks` |
| `layout.interleaved_mixed_types` | Interleaved channels of different fixed sizes (int16 next to float64) are read. | `interleaved_mixed_types` |
| `layout.interleaved_unequal_is_error` | Interleaved channels with different counts are a `TdmsFormatError`. | `interleaved_unequal_counts` |
| `layout.big_endian` | A segment with the big-endian flag is read completely: lead-in, metadata and data. | `big_endian`, `big_endian_interleaved` |
| `layout.mixed_endianness` | Segments of different byte order in one file are each read in their own. | `mixed_endianness` |
| `layout.channel_added_later` | A channel that first appears in a later segment starts there. | `new_list_replaces` |
| `layout.channel_dropped` | A channel that stops getting data keeps what it has. | `new_list_replaces` |

## Data types

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `type.integers` | int8 to int64 and uint8 to uint64 channels are read exactly, as native numpy arrays. | `integers`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms` |
| `type.floats` | float32 and float64 channels are read exactly, including NaN, inf and -0.0. | `floats`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `type.bool` | A boolean channel is read as a numpy bool array. | `booleans` |
| `type.string` | A string channel (offsets then text) is read, over several segments too, with empty and non-ASCII strings. | `strings` |
| `type.timestamp` | A timestamp channel is read as `datetime64[us]` (UTC, truncated). | `timestamps`, `timestamp_fraction_extremes` |
| `type.complex` | Complex single and double channels are read as complex64 and complex128. | `complex_numbers` |
| `type.no_data_type` | A channel that never has data has `dtype None`, length 0 and reads as an empty array (the quality_score channels). | `channel_without_data`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `type.unsupported_is_error` | A data type this package cannot read (extended float) is an `UnsupportedFeatureError`, not garbage. | `extended_float_channel` |

## Properties

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `prop.all_types` | Properties of every type (integers, floats, bool, string, timestamp, complex, with-unit floats) are read as Python values. | `property_types`, `property_complex`, `property_unit_types`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms` |
| `prop.root_group_channel` | Properties at the file, group and channel level are kept apart. | `minimal`, `property_types`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `prop.update` | A property written again in a later segment has the later value; others stay. | `property_update` |
| `prop.added_later` | A property that first appears in a later segment is there. | `property_update` |
| `prop.unicode` | Names and values with non-ASCII characters are read (UTF-8). | `property_unicode` |
| `prop.empty_and_odd_names` | An empty string value, a name with a trailing space and a very long value are kept as they are. | `property_odd_values`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `prop.timestamp_exact` | A timestamp property keeps seconds and the 2**-64 fraction exactly; conversion to `datetime64` truncates. | `timestamp_fraction_extremes`, `property_types` |
| `prop.many` | Thousands of properties on one object are read. | `many_properties` |
| `prop.unsupported_type_is_error` | A property of a type this package cannot read is an `UnsupportedFeatureError`. | `property_extended_float` |

## Objects and paths

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `path.group_without_channels` | A group that only has properties is a group with no channels. | `group_without_channels`, real: `one_int16_channel.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels.tdms`, real: `three_int16_channels_short.tdms`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `path.implicit_group` | A channel whose group object is never written still has its group. | `implicit_group` |
| `path.order` | Groups and channels are in the order of their first appearance in the file, not sorted. | `first_appearance_order` |
| `path.quote_and_slash` | Names with `'` (written `''`), `/` and spaces are read back as written. | `quotes_and_slashes` |
| `path.unicode` | Group and channel names with non-ASCII characters are read. | `property_unicode` |
| `path.reserved_looking_names` | Groups or channels named `info`, `name`, `groups`, `properties`, `data` or `read` are ordinary. | `reserved_looking_names`, real: `unequal_counts_untyped_channels.tdms` |
| `path.root_only_properties` | A file whose only object is the root has properties and no groups. | `root_only` |
| `path.invalid_is_error` | An object path that is not `/` or `/'group'` or `/'group'/'channel'` is a `TdmsFormatError`. | `three_level_path`, `path_without_slash` |

## Scaling

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `scale.linear` | A channel with one linear NI scale reads scaled, and raw with `scaled=False`. | `scale_linear` |
| `scale.polynomial` | A polynomial NI scale is applied. | `scale_polynomial` |
| `scale.chain` | Scales that take another scale as their input source are applied in that order. | `scale_chain` |
| `scale.already_scaled` | `NI_Scaling_Status` = `scaled` means the data is final and is not scaled again. | `scale_already_scaled` |
| `scale.group_level` | Scaling declared on the group applies to its channels without their own. | `scale_group_level` |
| `scale.file_level` | Scaling declared on the file applies to channels and groups without their own. | `scale_file_level` |
| `scale.channel_overrides_group` | A channel's own scaling wins over its group's. | `scale_channel_overrides_group` |
| `scale.float32_input` | Scaling single precision data is done in double precision and gives float64. | `scale_float32_input` |
| `scale.unsupported_is_error` | A scale type that is not implemented (RTD, thermocouple, ...) raises `UnsupportedScalingError` on a scaled read; the raw read works. | `scale_unsupported_type` |
| `scale.none` | A channel without scale properties reads the same scaled and raw. | `scale_channel_overrides_group`, `scale_none` |

## Unsupported layouts

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `daqmx.is_error` | DAQmx raw data (indexes 0x1269 and 0x126A) is an `UnsupportedFeatureError` that names DAQmx. | `daqmx_raw_data` |

## Robustness

| Case | The reader must | Exercised by |
|---|---|---|
| `robust.huge_counts` | Declared counts and lengths far beyond the file's size are a `TdmsFormatError` without allocating them. | `huge_object_count`, `huge_property_count`, `huge_string_length`, `huge_path_length`, `huge_value_count` |
| `robust.fuzz` | Truncated and randomly damaged files raise only `TdmsError` (never another exception, never hang, never allocate wildly). | `tests/test_fuzz.py::test_damaged_files_only_raise_tdms_errors` |
| `robust.lazy` | Opening a file reads its structure; channel data is read when asked for, and a slice reads only what it needs. | `tests/test_robust.py::test_opening_reads_the_structure_not_the_data` |
| `robust.large` | A file of 100 MB opens quickly and a channel reads in time proportional to its size (slow test). | `tests/test_robust.py::test_a_hundred_megabyte_channel_reads_in_proportion` |
| `robust.many_segments` | A file of tens of thousands of segments opens in a reasonable time. | `many_segments_5000` |
